terms.label: Inductance
terms.plain: Inductance tells how current stores magnetic energy.
terms.meaning: A scalar coil coefficient or symmetric inductance matrix, according to the attached contract.
cautions: Drawing diameter and turns are not a measured inductance.

terms.label: Mutual inductance
terms.plain: Changing current in one coil can induce voltage in another.
terms.meaning: The signed cross-coil coefficient; its sign depends on the chosen winding/dot convention.
cautions: Mutual coupling does not supply energy.

terms.label: Coupling coefficient
terms.plain: Coupling describes how strongly two modeled coils interact.
terms.meaning: In this passive positive-definite two-coil fixture, M = k√(L1 L2) and |k| < 1.
cautions: A selected k is not a measured coil calibration.

terms.label: Capacitance
terms.plain: A capacitor stores energy in an electric field.
terms.meaning: The capacitance coefficient; it is not the mathematical field of complex numbers ℂ.
cautions: C as capacitance differs from C used for coulombs or ℂ.

terms.label: Resistance and useful load
terms.plain: Resistance converts electrical energy to heat.
terms.meaning: The receiving load and winding/internal losses are accounted for separately.
cautions: R1 can also name a research round; ℝ denotes real numbers, not resistance.

terms.label: Electric charge
terms.plain: Charge measures how much electricity has accumulated.
terms.meaning: q is an instantaneous scalar or vector; its time derivative is current.
cautions: The unit C means coulomb here, not capacitance.

terms.label: Electrical current
terms.plain: Current is the flow rate of electric charge.
terms.meaning: Lowercase i(t) is instantaneous; uppercase I is a phasor whose peak/RMS convention must be declared.
cautions: The imaginary unit i in an impedance equation is a different meaning.

terms.label: Voltage and source-port drive
terms.plain: Voltage is electrical potential difference between two points.
terms.meaning: Instantaneous voltages and complex source-port phasors are distinct representations.
cautions: A source knob is not automatically a measured port voltage; declare peak or RMS.

terms.label: Angular frequency
terms.plain: Angular frequency counts how quickly a cycle turns through angle.
terms.meaning: One cycle is 2π radians, so ω = 2π f.
cautions: Radians per second and hertz differ by 2π.

terms.label: Impedance and reactance
terms.plain: Impedance describes opposition to an alternating current.
terms.meaning: Complex impedance combines resistance with reactive phase response; X = ωL − 1/(ωC) in the host series circuit.
cautions: Voltage magnification across storage elements is not power gain.

terms.label: Real average power
terms.plain: Power is the rate at which energy is transferred.
terms.meaning: Real average source power uses the real part of voltage times conjugate current, with a convention-dependent factor.
cautions: Peak phasors need a factor ½; RMS phasors do not.

terms.label: Stored energy
terms.plain: Energy can remain in the capacitor and magnetic field.
terms.meaning: Initial and final stored states belong in a finite-time source-work budget.
cautions: Released initial energy is not unexplained energy production.

terms.label: Work transferred over time
terms.plain: Work is energy transferred during a chosen interval.
terms.meaning: Integrating signed instantaneous power gives work; uppercase W here is a variable, while W after a number is the watt unit.
cautions: Lowercase w in the witness contract denotes a voltage, not work.

terms.label: Root mean square
terms.plain: RMS is the square root of the mean squared signal.
terms.meaning: For a pure sine only, peak amplitude is √2 times RMS. For a fixed resistor, RMS determines average heating.
cautions: RMS is not the arithmetic mean or a universal peak conversion.

terms.label: Peak amplitude
terms.plain: Peak amplitude is the largest excursion from zero.
terms.meaning: The imported R1/R2/R3 electrical phasors use peak amplitude, while the host circuit inputs use RMS.
cautions: Sample peak, reconstructed true peak and acoustic pressure peak are different measurements.

terms.label: Not to scale
terms.plain: A sketch may show relationships without preserving size ratios.
terms.meaning: Use written dimensions and declared coordinate units rather than measuring screen pixels.
cautions: An accurate-looking diagram is not an engineering drawing or a calibrated photograph.

terms.label: Estimate, difference and time derivative
terms.plain: Marks over a symbol tell you which version, change or bound is meant.
terms.meaning: A hat denotes an estimate; δ often a difference or perturbation; Δ can denote a final-minus-initial change or a supplied error bound, according to the contract; a dot is a time derivative.
cautions: Δa and ΔM in these contracts are error-bound radii, not temporal changes. Every symbol needs declared units; ż is velocity, not position.

terms.label: Matrix, transpose, diagonal and inverse
terms.plain: A matrix collects several linked equations into one map.
terms.meaning: Transpose T swaps rows/columns; diag forms a diagonal matrix; inverse undoes an invertible map.
cautions: A matrix inverse is not defined at a singular parameter choice.

equations.title: Peak and RMS are different conventions
equations.plain: For a sine across a resistor, 1 V peak gives half the heating power of 1 V RMS at the same resistance.
equations.convention: Pure sinusoid; ideal fixed resistor; upstream phasors peak, host circuit input RMS.
equations.units: V, Ω, W; at R=1 Ω: 1 V peak →0.5 W, 1 V RMS →1 W.
cautions: Do not apply the √2 conversion to arbitrary waveforms.

equations.title: Account for all source work
equations.equation: Win = Wload + Wloss + ΔE; E = ½ iᵀLi + ½ qᵀdiag(1/C)q
equations.plain: Source work goes to useful load, heating losses and a change of stored energy.
equations.convention: Instantaneous states and signed finite-time work; no RMS substitution into instantaneous storage.
equations.units: Each work/storage term J; i A, q C, L H, capacitance F.
cautions: Initial stored energy is included. Voltage gain alone is not surplus energy.

handbook.title: Series RLC: source, load and stored energy
handbook.kind: exact SVG circuit and measurement-boundary diagram
handbook.overview: Exact R3 model topology; a physical measurement arrangement is proposed and unbuilt. Voltage gain can exceed one while source work closes against load heat, internal loss and storage change. Probe symbols indicate waveform acquisition, not slow-meter readings; real sensor loading and bandwidth need characterization.
handbook.goal: Follow one series resistance–inductance–capacitance energy account and see why a large component voltage need not imply energy gain.
signalSteps: A declared source supplies current through the series circuit.
Resistance dissipates energy while inductance and capacitance store and return energy.
Integrate signed source power and compare load heat, internal losses and the storage change.
